summary: Interpreted the witness receipt and closed the verify question's open gap. In all six trials a successor led at term 3 before the verdict (first sampled at 319-454ms) while the old leader stayed at term 2, and in three of them (parsed indices 3, 7 and 9) VerifyLeader returned success at 931ms — the moment the 900ms store stall released the main loop, by which time the non-voter's acknowledgement had already been counted on a replication goroutine; the other three answered 'leadership lost while committing log'. The distinguishing step versus the earlier refuted child question is registration order: a request queued during the stall cannot be registered, so this probe registers first and stalls afterwards, which is what lets the vote be counted while the lease check cannot run. The gap answer is now resolved with that stated condition, the counterevidence rewritten so the lease is described as protecting only the running-loop case, a new Fact records the witness, and joint history explains how the two harnesses compose (same build, topology and timeouts; the later one adds the condition). The parent defect claim is unchanged; only its consequence moves from conditional to observed. No execution requested. Remaining: the caller's FSM read is still not exercised, and the stall and reconnection remain supplied conditions.
